title: AgenticMail MCP HTTP mode -- T1190 unauthenticated /mcp exposes master-key tools
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-50287 (GHSA-63gr-g7jc-v8rg,
CVSS 8.7 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for `@agenticmail/mcp`, prior
to 0.9.27.

When started with `--http` or `MCP_HTTP=1`, `packages/mcp/src/index.ts`
launches an HTTP server for the `/mcp` endpoint with no Authorization
header validation. An unauthenticated client can send an `initialize`
JSON-RPC request, receive an `mcp-session-id` in response with no
credential exchanged, and then invoke `tools/call` directly. Separately,
`packages/mcp/src/tools.ts` marks certain gateway/admin operations as
requiring the operator's `AGENTICMAIL_MASTER_KEY`, but the server
executes them with its OWN server-side master key regardless of caller
authentication -- a confused-deputy shape, same class as this corpus's
`observed_mcp_pinot_unauth_confused_deputy_t1190`. The exposed
master-key tools include `setup_email_relay`, `setup_email_domain`,
`delete_agent`, `cleanup_agents`, and `send_test_email`.

This is the SAME product family as
`observed_agenticmail_bridge_wake_unverified_sender_t1566` already in
this corpus, but a distinct vulnerability and code path -- that rule
targets the email-triggered bridge-wake flow (`dispatcher.ts`), this
one targets the MCP HTTP transport's own auth gap (`index.ts`).

Detection logic flags an unauthenticated `tools/call` request naming
one of the master-key-protected tools -- the tool name plus missing
Authorization header is the discriminator, since the same tool names
legitimately appear in authenticated traffic once the fix is deployed.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (agenticmail,
via GHSA and NVD), fixed in 0.9.27 (requires bearer tokens/shared
secrets for `/mcp` HTTP requests and disables master-key tools over
unauthenticated transports).
